batch_note: Seed data for the Public Policy Explorer. All markets are state=proposed: they are sitting in the listing pipeline and no staking is possible until governance lists them. Topics are draft placeholders pending founder sign-off (SPEC decision D-9).

markets.title: Should Congress codify the Presidential transition briefing timeline?
markets.summary_plain: By law, presidential candidates get security briefings and transition resources after the election. Some rules about timing are tradition, not law. This market asks whether Congress will pass a bill that writes those timing rules into law during the current two-year session.
markets.condition: This market resolves YES if and only if a bill that establishes a statutory deadline for post-election presidential transition briefings and access is enacted (signed into law) before this market's deadline. Resolves NO otherwise.
markets.resolution_source: The enacted-bill listing for the current Congress on congress.gov, plus the White House signing statements page

markets.title: Will Congress pass an annual appropriations package before the fiscal deadline?
markets.summary_plain: Each year Congress must fund the government before the fiscal year starts on October 1. When it doesn't, parts of the government shut down. This market asks whether a full-year funding package will be enacted before the next deadline.
markets.condition: This market resolves YES if and only if a full-year appropriations act covering the affected fiscal year is enacted before the market deadline. A continuing resolution alone does not count as YES.
markets.resolution_source: The public laws listing on congress.gov for the applicable fiscal year

markets.title: Will Congress raise the federal minimum wage this session?
markets.summary_plain: The federal minimum wage has been $7.25 per hour since 2009. Several bills to raise it have been introduced over the years. This market asks whether any bill raising the federal minimum wage will become law during the current session of Congress.
markets.condition: This market resolves YES if and only if an enacted law raising the federal minimum wage above $7.25 per hour is signed before the market deadline. State or local changes do not count.
markets.resolution_source: The enacted-bills listing for the current Congress on congress.gov

markets.title: Will Congress pass a federal data-privacy law for consumer data?
markets.summary_plain: Right now, rules about how companies handle your personal data differ from state to state. Several comprehensive federal privacy bills have been proposed. This market asks whether one becomes law during the current session.
markets.condition: This market resolves YES if and only if a comprehensive federal consumer data-privacy act is enacted before the market deadline. Sector-specific rules (e.g., health or financial data only) do not count.
markets.resolution_source: The enacted-bills listing for the current Congress on congress.gov

markets.title: Will a federal election-administration funding bill be enacted?
markets.summary_plain: Elections in the US are run by states, but Congress can send money to help states pay for election equipment, security, and administration. This market asks whether a dedicated election-administration funding bill becomes law during the current session.
markets.condition: This market resolves YES if and only if an enacted law that appropriates federal funds specifically for election administration is signed before the market deadline. General emergency or omnibus spending without election-specific appropriations does not count.
markets.resolution_source: The enacted-bills listing for the current Congress on congress.gov
